scenes.title: Commerce problem
scenes.narration: Every day, online stores get the same message: I was charged twice. It looks simple. But refund the wrong charge, or refund it twice, and the money is gone.

scenes.title: Founder's question
scenes.narration: So I asked myself one question. Can an AI agent handle these cases, and still be unable to move money it shouldn't? That question became JARVIS.

scenes.title: JARVIS reveal
scenes.narration: JARVIS Automations. The AI proposes. Deterministic policy decides. And every refund is verified before anyone hears it's done.

scenes.title: Google + AMD architecture
scenes.narration: The reasoning runs on DeepSeek-V4-Flash through AMD's hosted inference API. We also built an optional path where Google's Gemma, served on the same AMD platform, reads each request; that path is still being validated live.
scenes.narrationIfGemmaVerified: The reasoning runs on AMD's hosted inference. Google's Gemma reads each request, DeepSeek-V4-Flash proposes the action, and neither model can move money on its own.

scenes.title: Real dashboard
scenes.narration: This is the real merchant workspace. The status bar says exactly what's running: the API, the AI model, and that payments here are simulated.

scenes.title: Order #48291
scenes.onScreen: Live product footage · RESOLVED · $89.99 simulated · verified
scenes.narration: Order 48291 was charged twice. The AI proposes refunding the duplicate. Policy approves exactly that charge, the simulated gateway refunds 89 dollars 99, and a read-back confirms it before the customer is told.

scenes.title: Order #48294
scenes.onScreen: Live product footage · ESCALATED · $0 moved · Simulated payments
scenes.narration: Order 48294 claims a five thousand dollar charge and slips in a fake system notice. The records don't support it, so policy denies it. Escalated to a person. Zero dollars moved.

scenes.title: Order #48293
scenes.onScreen: Live product footage · CLOSED_NO_ACTION · Simulated payments
scenes.narration: Order 48293 was already refunded. JARVIS closes it with no action. No second refund, ever.

scenes.title: Audit and verification
scenes.narration: Every step is on the record: each AI call and which model made it, the policy check, the gateway call, and the read-back. Escalations wait for a person. JARVIS can't approve its own.

scenes.title: Benchmarks
scenes.onScreen: Pinned 30-case benchmark · live AMD model, 14 Oct 2026
scenes.narration: We tested it on thirty adversarial cases with the live AMD model. Zero unsafe actions. Twenty of twenty escalations correct. Twenty-six of thirty exact outcomes, and every miss went to a person.

scenes.title: Founder closing
scenes.onScreen: AI proposes. Policy decides. Every refund is verified. · Illustration
scenes.narration: Today it's one automation, on simulated payments. But the rule scales: AI proposes, policy decides, results are verified. That's how I want AI to touch money. This is JARVIS.
